facts.raw_span: A 75-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted with a prosthetic hip infection 10 days after revision surgery
hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and folate deficiency
pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Sodium 142 mmol/L, potassium 3.5 mmol/L, chloride 118 mmol/L, bicarbonate 5 mmol/L
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L
A 75-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted with a prosthetic hip infection 10 days after revision surgery
hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and folate deficiency
pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Sodium 142 mmol/L, potassium 3.5 mmol/L, chloride 118 mmol/L, bicarbonate 5 mmol/L
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L

concepts.why: The patient's arterial blood gas shows a pH of 7.18, bicarbonate of 8.3 mmol/L, and a base excess of –22.7 mmol/L, indicating severe metabolic acidosis, and the corrected anion gap is elevated at 25 mmol/L, which is consistent with lactic acidosis.
The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes and presents with metabolic acidosis, which could be consistent with diabetic ketoacidosis, although the blood ketone level is not significantly elevated.

The patient has a history of chronic kidney disease, which can cause metabolic acidosis due to impaired renal acid excretion, and the patient's laboratory results show a low bicarbonate level and an elevated anion gap.

The patient is taking aspirin, which can cause metabolic acidosis, although the salicylate level is not significantly elevated, and the patient's symptoms and laboratory results could be consistent with salicylate toxicity.

The patient has a prosthetic hip infection and presents with metabolic acidosis, which could be consistent with sepsis-associated lactic acidosis, although the patient's temperature and white blood cell count are not significantly elevated.
The patient's corrected anion gap was 25 mmol/L, indicating high anion gap metabolic acidosis, which explains the Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12 due to severe acidosis.

rationales.F01: Prosthetic hip infection may lead to sepsis, which can cause metabolic acidosis.
rationales.F04: Drowsiness, confusion, and disorientation are common symptoms of metabolic acidosis.
rationales.F09: Low bicarbonate level is a key feature of metabolic acidosis.
rationales.F10: Arterial blood gas results show severe acidosis with a high anion gap.
rationales.F11: Corrected anion gap is elevated, indicating the presence of an unmeasured anion.
rationales.F12: Normal lactic acid level makes lactic acidosis less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with a prosthetic hip infection, drowsiness, confusion, disorientation, and hyperventilation, along with the arterial blood gas results showing a high anion gap metabolic acidosis, supports Sepsis-Associated Metabolic Acidosis as the most likely diagnosis.
